claims.text: Explicitly incorporating defects and impurities through advanced simulation will produce more accurate electronic-conductivity estimates for bulk HfNbTaTiZr than traditional analytical predictions based on perfect crystals.
The modeled bulk HfNbTaTiZr has realistic point defects and compositional disorder.
One modeled specimen is near-pure HfNbTaTiZr and another contains 1 wt.% oxygen.
The predictive method will represent realistic defect distributions and oxygen-impurity effects in its conductivity calculations.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials can be trained on ab initio data sampling defect configurations for this application.
Quantum effects and impurity scattering dominate electronic conductivity in the nearly 0–200 K regime.
Thermal disorder and phonon scattering are significant in the 300–1200 K regime.
Point defects and 1 wt.% oxygen alter the electronic-scattering environment relative to a perfect HfNbTaTiZr crystal.
Including realistic defects and impurity interactions accounts for additional electronic-scattering channels.
Local structural variations caused by defects and impurities strongly influence electronic conductivity.
Representing the true physicochemical state of the material will improve agreement between predicted and measured conductivity.
The proposed approach will predict conductivity within approximately 10% of measurements in both specified temperature regimes.
Standard analytical models typically have conductivity errors larger than 10% for these specimens and temperature regimes.
Current analytical conductivity predictions assume ideal, defect-free crystals.
Neglecting defects and oxygen causes significant disagreement between analytical predictions and experimental conductivity data.
The framework is expected to be reliable for bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing up to 1 wt.% oxygen from near 0 K to 1200 K.
The framework's accuracy above 1 wt.% oxygen or outside the stated temperature range is not established.
A conductivity error greater than approximately 10% in either specified temperature regime, or failure to reproduce the observed oxygen/defect trend, will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The conditions define applicability only for 0–200 K and 300–1200 K, leaving 200–300 K unaddressed, whereas the boundary claims reliability continuously from near 0 K through 1200 K.
